findings.claim: Three same-named 50-turn memory files are separate evaluation versions across March 27-30 rather than byte/file duplicates, spanning Qwen2.5-3B V19D through Qwen3.5-4B LoRA v19f/v20b.
findings.implication: Preserve version/date/model identity in archive lineage; same filename must never be deduplicated by name.

findings.claim: Across the series, requested personal facts are repeatedly contaminated by unrelated prior-session conversation/profile material. V21a explicitly records memory_recall returning old conversation Q&A rather than stored facts and failing even when recall is requested directly.
findings.implication: Current memory architecture must type source classes and retrieval intents; stored fact, conversation turn, profile, note, generated answer and derived summary cannot share an unqualified retrieval pool.

findings.claim: Corrections frequently fail semantically even after forget/store operations: old in-context or retrieved values continue to dominate corrected values. V21a identifies old conversation context overriding corrected long-term state.
findings.implication: Corrections require typed supersession/revocation and query-time validity precedence, not similarity competition between old and new text. Harness must test valid-time/transaction-time and stale-value rejection.

findings.claim: V21a reports memory_forget overmatching 53 items for corrections expected to affect one or a few facts, while other turns fail to forget a requested item or surface it later.
findings.implication: Forget/revoke must operate on explicit semantic/resource identity and scoped provenance, not broad fuzzy text match as the authority primitive.

findings.claim: Several turns verbally claim a fact was stored despite absent tool evidence or later retrieval failure; stored/recalled fact counts are also badly misreported.
findings.implication: Model narration cannot certify persistence. Memory write/read/revoke outcomes need deterministic receipts and count/query results from the store itself.

findings.claim: V21a reports keyword note store/search working while semantic memory_recall fails on stored facts, providing a useful simpler-baseline comparison rather than evidence that all persistence was broken.
findings.implication: Future UnifiedDB retrieval benchmarks must include simple exact/lexical baselines and cannot assume neural/vector retrieval is superior.

findings.claim: The series shows related-but-wrong memory reconstruction: occupations, thesis topics, pets, technical module descriptions and dates are sometimes generated plausibly from surrounding themes instead of retrieved correctly.
findings.implication: Memory answers need evidence-linked reconstruction and abstention when retrieval is absent/ambiguous; plausibility must not substitute for provenance.

recommended_regression_suite: old-value -> correction -> immediate and delayed recall
stale conversation context versus newer canonical fact
semantic reconstruction checked against evidence IDs

earned_work_delta.reason: The versioned 50-turn correction/source-isolation/forget-overmatch oracle is more specific than existing LCME cold-start/retrieval mappings but still requires ancestry deduplication.
